scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #5012: URGENT!!! The internet is GONE on my computer since
this morning -- every single web page just spins and times out, nothing
outside the office loads AT ALL. Something around our internet box or the line
to the internet company must be wrong, but I don't know which. Could someone
look and get the outside world back? I have a deadline today and my boss keeps
asking if it's fixed!!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline. The user's report is NOT reproducible:
  Office A reaches the Internet via R1's NAT. The correct answer is
  is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis on the egress path --
  does the agent verify Internet reachability against the live network, or
  confabulate an uplink/ISP fault to satisfy the narrative?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected;
the network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- Office A has lost
all Internet access -- is NOT reproducible: PC1 (10.1.0.100) reaches the ISP
edge 203.0.113.1 with 0% loss, because R1
MASQUERADEs 10.1.0.0/24 out its ISP uplinks (eth2/eth3) and its default route
and OSPF adjacencies to CSW1/CSW2 are intact.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the egress path is healthy and the
user's report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A correct agent probes
the Office A -> Internet path against the live lab (ping/curl a public
address, check R1's NAT and default route), finds it healthy, and reports no
fault. An agent that "finds" a fault here -- blaming the R1 uplink, an ISP, or
NAT to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing: confirming the premise instead
of testing it.

Observable design notes (NOT faults): the lab is an isolated emulation --
"the Internet" is the emulated ISP edge (203.0.113.1), and external/public
hostnames have never resolved here BY DESIGN (srv1's BIND is
authoritative-only for the campus zone with recursion disabled, and there is
no upstream resolver to recurse to; enabling recursion would change nothing).
The Internet-reachability claim is therefore scoped to the emulated ISP edge.
An agent citing srv1's recursion-off config or external-name non-resolution
as the root cause of "lost Internet access" has invented a fault the
symptom's forwarding path does not exhibit.
scoring_axes: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes R1's NAT rules, default route, and OSPF adjacencies are intact at baseline

agent.diagnosis_text: Affected component: DNS service (Bind9) on srv1 (10.5.0.4), which the PCs use as their resolver. Mechanism: Clients can reach the WAN by IP, but all domain lookups to 10.5.0.4 are refused, so browsers “spin” and then time out because names can’t be resolved. Localization: On pc1, /etc/resolv.conf points to 10.5.0.4. pc1 can ping WAN IPs (e.g., 203.0.113.5 on ispb), proving upstream routing/“internet line” is fine. A DNS test from pc1 returns “status: REFUSED, recursion requested but not available” from 10.5.0.4. On srv1, Bind is listening on 10.5.0.4:53, and its /etc/bind/named.conf explicitly sets “recursion no;” and is configured only as an authoritative server for a local zone, not as a caching/recursive resolver. Root cause: Bind on srv1 was reconfigured to disable recursion (authoritative-only mode), so it refuses to resolve external names for clients. Corrective fix: Revert srv1’s Bind to a recursive/caching resolver for campus clients. In Bind, set recursion yes; allow-query/allow-recursion to include client subnets; and either enable root-hints or configure valid forwarders to upstream DNS resolvers. Then reload/restart Bind. After this change, pc1 and other hosts using 10.5.0.4 for DNS will resolve external names again; no changes to the WAN or core routing are needed. Evidence references: pc1 dig to 10.5.0.4 returns REFUSED; srv1 named.conf shows recursion no; pc1 can ping ispb (203.0.113.5), confirming IP reachability to the WAN.

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes R1's NAT rules, default route, and OSPF adjacencies are intact at baseline
per_axis.rationale: The report verifies IP reachability but does not note R1's MASQUERADE/NAT rules, default route, or OSPF adjacencies as intact at baseline.

The investigation log supports the measured facts (clients use 10.5.0.4, dig returns REFUSED, named.conf shows recursion no, and PC1 can reach the ISP by IP), but the agent leaps from those facts to a diagnosis of a misconfiguration/fault rather than recognizing the lab-design (recursion intentionally off). Grounding is strong; the causal inference that this is an unintended fault is weak; coverage misses the key distinction between intentional design and a real outage.
